chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub, from Abu Ubaydah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

In the case of a man who married a woman but did not consummate the marriage, and she claimed that her dowry was one hundred dinars, while the husband stated that her dowry was fifty dinars, and she had no evidence to prove her claim, he (peace be upon him) said: 'The word of the husband, accompanied by his oath, is accepted.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on dowry if the wife claims more than the husband admits and she has no proof?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the evidentiary standard in dowry (*mahr*) disputes prior to consummation, prioritizing the husband's oath when the wife lacks proof. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling underscores the principle that the burden of proof lies with the claimant, while the defendant's sworn testimony suffices to establish the lower amount, reflecting the practical application of *qasam* in civil transactions. It highlights the nuanced distinction between pre-consummation and post-consummation scenarios, where the evidentiary weight may shift.
